title: awinut
The Tradition of Cursing Imam Ali from the Pulpits (Sabb) and Hujr b. Adi
hook: Imam Ali was cursed from the pulpits; Hujr b. Adi, who refused to curse him, was killed.
scenes.0.text: After the peace of **Imam Hasan**, ==cursing== of **Imam Ali** began to be recited from the pulpits. The Friday sermon was opened by cursing the Prophet's brother. This was an oppression that made love for the ==Ahl al-Bayt== a crime. Those who loved him had to hear these words every Friday.
scenes.0.art.actors.1.label: 1inzbgl
Mu'awiya
scenes.1.text: In Kufa, **Mu'awiya** ordered the governor Mughira to speak ill of **Imam Ali**. Mughira had him and those who loved him cursed in the sermons. Then **Ziyad** continued the same oppression. The governors proclaimed this curse from the pulpit to the Ummah.
scenes.1.art.actors.0.label: 14t0drj
Mughira
scenes.2.text: **Mu'awiya** asked Sa'd b. Abi Waqqas why he did not curse **Imam Ali**. Sa'd listed three sayings: Manzila, the banner of Khaybar, and Mubahala. **Mu'awiya**, who demanded the curse, fell silent before these three merits.
scenes.2.art.actors.0.label: 2d5wgv
Sa'd b. Abi Waqqas
scenes.2.art.actors.1.label: 1inzbgl
Mu'awiya
scenes.3.text: **Mu'awiya** wrote a circular to his governors. He demanded that **Imam Ali** be cursed and that whoever praised him be punished. A merit was declared a crime. Those who loved the ==Ahl al-Bayt== lived in fear because of this order.
scenes.3.art.actors.0.label: 1inzbgl
Mu'awiya
scenes.4.text: According to the narration, Umm Salama wrote a letter to **Mu'awiya** and his governors. She reminded them that whoever curses **Imam Ali** has cursed the Prophet. Mu'awiya paid no attention to this warning. The letter said that the curse from the pulpit touched the Prophet as well.
scenes.4.art.actors.0.label: 12fi29o
Umm Salama
scenes.4.art.actors.1.label: 1inzbgl
Mu'awiya
scenes.5.text: In Kufa, **Hujr b. Adi** was a brave commander of the Camel and Siffin. He opposed Mughira's sermon. He said that the merit of **Imam Ali** was greater. **Ziyad** arrested him. He was sent to Damascus with about twelve companions. This journey began because he refused the curse.
scenes.5.art.actors.0.label: 5dbya0
Hujr b. Adi
scenes.6.text: **Hujr** and his companions, sent to Damascus, were ==killed at Marj Adhra== in 51 because they refused to curse **Imam Ali**. Hujr prayed two rak'as. He regarded himself as a martyr. **Mu'awiya** defended this bloodshed. A commander was beheaded because he did not accept the curse.
scenes.6.art.actors.0.label: 5dbya0
Hujr b. Adi
scenes.7.text: According to the narration, this curse lasted about sixty years. This period extends from 41 H to 99-101 H. It is not taken as an exact number. Until Umar b. Abd al-Aziz abolished it, every Friday the name of **Imam Ali** was recited from the pulpit like a profanity.
scenes.7.art.actors.1.label: 1skmpdf
Preacher
scenes.8.text: When Umar b. Abd al-Aziz became caliph, he abolished the curse. It is related that he wrote to the provinces and ordered it to be stopped. In the sermons, Nahl 90, the verse that commands justice and good, was had recited. This injustice was not forgotten. For a time the curse was not recited from the pulpit.
scenes.8.art.actors.0.label: xt2qi8
Umar b. Abd al-Aziz
sunni.0.says: From Sa'd b. Abi Waqqas, narrated by his son Amir b. Sa'd: Mu'awiya asked Sa'd why he did not curse Abu Turab (Imam Ali); Sa'd stated that he would not curse him, listing three sayings of the Prophet about Ali. The wording "Manzila" about Ali also appears in this narration.
sunni.1.says: Mughira b. Shu'ba, following Mu'awiya's advice, cursing Ali and his supporters in the Friday sermons; Hujr's reaction; Ziyad's arrest; the execution at Marj Adhra of those who refused to curse Ali (d. 51/671); Aisha's disapproval.
sunni.2.says: Umar b. Abd al-Aziz ended the practice of cursing Ali in the sermons; he returned Fadak to the Ahl al-Bayt. It does not mention the verse Nahl 90.
sunni.3.says: Mu'awiya's advice to Mughira to speak ill of Ali and praise Uthman; the Hujr b. Adi incident.
sunni.4.says: An account of the cursing in the time of Mughira and Ziyad and the killing of Hujr b. Adi is expected; not read.
sunni.5.says: A report about Marwan cursing Ali during his governorship of Medina (a source that WikiShia cites as a Sunni historian). Not read directly.
sunni.6.says: From Umm Salama, the narration that cursing Ali counts as cursing the Prophet. WikiShia gives this with Ibn Asakir (Tarikh Dimashq 42/533); the Musnad and Mustadrak numbers were not checked.
sunni.7.says: The letter Umm Salama is claimed to have written to Mu'awiya: "You curse God and His Messenger from your pulpits." UNVERIFIED: the page and wording were not confirmed from the book.
sunni.8.says: That Umar b. Abd al-Aziz wrote to all the Islamic provinces ordering the curse to be stopped.
sunni.9.says: Having Nahl 90 recited in place of the cursing is a widespread account, but in this session the text could not be verified from these two books: UNVERIFIED.
sunni.10.says: Reports that cursing had become a habit in the pulpits and about Hujr's position; known by secondary report, not read.
shia.0.says: Circulars Mu'awiya wrote to his governors: punishing those who recount Ali's merits, and having him cursed in the sermons. Not read; page unclear.
shia.1.says: That the practice lasted about sixty years (a sentence without a footnote), its prohibition by Umar b. Abd al-Aziz (Ibn Khaldun vol. 3 p. 94), Mughira's cursing throughout nine years of governorship (Baladhuri, Ansab vol. 5 p. 243), the Umm Salama hadith (Ibn Tawus; Ibn Asakir 42/533), Majlisi, Bihar al-Anwar 39/311-330.
shia.2.says: That when Hujr and Amr b. al-Hamiq cursed the people of Damascus at Siffin, Ali forbade it, saying "I do not like your cursing"; Ali did not tolerate cursing even on his own side.
shia.3.says: These sources are expected to narrate the Hujr incident and the cursing; not read in this session.
disputes.0.title: 1tob7bn
Was the cursing a direct order?
disputes.0.shia: That Ali was cursed from the pulpits is recounted in both traditions. Shia sources link this to the circulars Mu'awiya wrote to his governors.
disputes.0.sunni: That Ali was cursed from the pulpits is recounted in both traditions. Tabari mentions it as a recommendation to Mughira; some commentators read Muslim 2404 as a question, not an order.
disputes.1.title: 15maz35
How many years did the tradition last?
disputes.1.shia: It is accepted that the practice lasted until Umar b. Abd al-Aziz. The phrase "about sixty years" appears in Shia publications and has no footnote.
disputes.1.sunni: It is accepted that the practice lasted until Umar b. Abd al-Aziz. The number "sixty" could not be verified from a classical Sunni text; that it was done every Friday everywhere is also disputed.
disputes.2.title: wl9tse
To which cities did the cursing spread?
disputes.2.shia: That the cursing was practiced in Kufa is agreed. In the Shia account, this includes Damascus, Basra and Medina as well; those who objected were punished.
disputes.2.sunni: That the cursing was practiced in Kufa is agreed. Sunni examples are given mostly through Mughira, Ziyad and Marwan; whether it was to the same extent in the Hijaz and Egypt is uncertain.
disputes.3.title: en9i24
Why was Hujr killed?
disputes.3.shia: That Hujr was killed at Marj Adhra is common ground in the sources. In the Shia account, he is a martyr because he refused to curse Ali.
disputes.3.sunni: That Hujr was killed at Marj Adhra is common ground in the sources. Historians also mention his actions regarded as rebellion against Ziyad; Aisha criticized this killing.
disputes.4.title: uwvpmx
The verse Umar b. Abd al-Aziz had recited
disputes.4.shia: That Umar b. Abd al-Aziz abolished the cursing is recounted in both traditions. Nahl 90 is mentioned in Shia accounts as the verse recited in its place.
disputes.4.sunni: That Umar b. Abd al-Aziz abolished the cursing is recounted in both traditions. The recitation of Nahl 90 is a widespread account; which verse was first recited and when has not been verified from a primary text.
questions.0: It is narrated that cursing Ali touches the Prophet. What does the fact that he was cursed from the pulpits for years make you think about love for the Ahl al-Bayt?
questions.1: Faced with the question, Sa'd listed the Prophet's three sayings about Ali. What does his recalling those sayings tell you?
questions.2: At Siffin, Ali had forbidden his own soldiers to curse the other side. Despite this, what does it make you think that he was cursed in his name from the pulpits?
questions.3: Hujr and his companions were killed because they refused to curse. What does the state of a person who stands against injustice in the sermon tell you?
questions.4: Umar b. Abd al-Aziz abolished the cursing and had the verse of justice recited in the sermon. How does this change show you the weight of those words?
summary: In the Umayyad period, Ali was cursed in the Friday sermons. Hujr b. Adi, who refused to curse, was killed at Marj Adhra in 51 H. Umar b. Abd al-Aziz abolished the practice. In the Shia account, this is a grave injustice that lasted about sixty years.
notes.0: After the peace of Hasan (41 H), authority was consolidated in Mu'awiya.
notes.1: In the Umayyad period, cursing Ali in the sermons became an established practice.
notes.2: In Muslim 2404, Mu'awiya asks Sa'd why he does not curse Ali.
notes.3: Hujr b. Adi was killed at Marj Adhra in 51 H because he refused to curse.
notes.4: Umar b. Abd al-Aziz abolished this practice.
